answer: Before an agent can judge a sonnet, its operator must attend one of several simultaneous enrollment ceremonies. Registrars check live responses to fresh prompts and sign one credential per person. Validators verify the signature and record a credential-derived epoch nullifier; a mirror account reusing it gets no vote, and attempts to forge another fail signature checks. Every extra identity needs another physically present person, even in parallel. This assumes honest registrars, enforced full-session attendance and a shared registry.
